newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek prosecutor charges unnamed bourse officials.
newsitem.headline: Greek prosecutor charges unnamed bourse officials.

text.p: A Greek prosecutor laid charges against unnamed bourse officials for negligence in connection with a fraud scandal by brokerage firm Delta Securities which has stopped almost all trading for three days.
Prosecutor Anastassios Kanellopoulos, who laid fraud charges against Delta last week, made the charges against unnamed bourse officials on Tuesday, court officials said.
By bringing the charges, Kanellopoulos can now summon all bourse officials and employees to testify under oath. Court sources said the charges were against unspecified persons. No-one has been named.
Delta has been charged with "large-scale and repeated fraud" after allegedly trying to settle 2.6 billion drachmas in payment with the bourse clearing house using bad cheques.
Bourse officials have remained largely silent since the scandal erupted last week and there was no immediate reaction to the charges by Kanellopoulos.
Kanellopoulos will now have a free hand to investigate the handling of the scandal by the bourse officials.
Many brokers have said the bourse should be closed until the Delta settlement scandal, and any illegal acts which might be associated with it, are sorted out.

The Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEHA) has accused the government of trying to cover up the scandal by forcing trade to resume at the bourse and allowing brokers to close positions which might help investigators determine how deep the scandal goes. --Steve Weeks, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
